0.note: A conclusion was reached and the envelope carries it.

1.note: A negative conclusion was reached. The envelope still carries it and is still the source of truth; the exit code alone is not read as the verdict.

2.note: Input unreadable, or nothing was evaluated. This release deliberately exits 2 rather than 0 when its status is NOT_EVALUATED, so a directory it could not assess never reports success.

interpreter.positiveEvidence: denominator.scored > 0 — at least one required-level rule was actually scored. This release reports denominator.scored at the run level with basis 'required-level rules that were evaluated', so a run in which every rule was skipped as not-applicable is visible as scored: 0 and cannot support a positive conclusion.

knownHazards.hazard: The envelope carries a numeric score alongside status. Reading score without first reading status invites a plausible-looking percentage from a run that concluded nothing.
knownHazards.mitigation: score is never read. The conclusion comes from status, and whether it is supported comes from the interpreter's evidence gate.

knownHazards.hazard: Invoking through the pack's npm scripts would apply its own default target rather than the project under evaluation.
knownHazards.mitigation: The entry point is invoked directly with an absolute --dir.
